section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) as the measure used: participants answered the 10-item BAS-2 on a 5-point scale. It reports that the BAS-2 is one-dimensional with good internal reliability (Cronbach  = .91–.94) and 3-week stability (r = .90) in samples of college and community women and men, and cites Halliwell et al. (2015) finding good reliability (Cronbach  = .94–.95) among 14- and 15-year-old girls. The section does not mention study labels such as 'Study 1' nor provide sample size, demographics, BMI, or data collection method for the present study.
section_summary.evidence_source: Participants answered the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015a), a 10-item scale measuring positive body image. All items are answered on a 5-point scale, ranging from 1 (Never) to 5 (Always). The BAS-2 is composed of one dimension with good internal reliability (Cronbach  = .91–.94) and 3-week stability, r = .90 in samples of college and community women and men (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015a; Webb, 2015). Halliwell et al. (2015) found good internal reliability (Cronbach  = .94–.95) in BAS-2 scores among a group of 14- and 15-year-old girls.
